revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Bridge Engineering
revealWordProblem.text: The Golden Gate Bridge's two main cables are each about 7,650 feet long. A supply company sells cable-protection wrap in spools measured in yards. How many yards of protective wrap does one full cable need? Show your work using a conversion factor.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: 1 yard = 3 feet, so converting feet to the larger unit (yards) means dividing by the conversion factor: 7,650 ÷ 3 = 2,550 yards. One cable needs 2,550 yards of protective wrap.

conceptIntro.heading: Let's build it together — How do I change one measurement unit into another?
conceptIntro.intro: A unit is a standard amount used to measure, like a foot or an inch. A conversion factor is a ratio that relates two units, like 1 foot = 12 inches. We'll walk through a worked example, try one together, then you'll try a few with hints right there when you need them.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Multiply when changing to a smaller unit, and divide when changing to a bigger unit.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: The cabinet is 5 feet tall. I want to know how many inches that is.
My conversion factor is 1 foot = 12 inches.
Inches are smaller than feet, so I multiply: 5 × 12 = 60.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: A wire is 4 yards long. The factor is 1 yard = 3 feet.
Feet are smaller than yards, so do we multiply or divide? (Multiply)
Now a metric example: a power cable is 3 meters long. The factor is 1 meter = 100 centimeters.
Centimeters are smaller than meters, so we multiply: 3 × 100 = 300 centimeters.
Sentence frame — say it with me: "The multiples/steps I need are ___ , and the answer is ___ ."

youDo.title: Now you try — with support
lines: Try the practice problems below. The hint button is right there whenever you get stuck — use it, that's smart.

discourse.prompt: How do you decide whether to multiply or divide when converting units?
discourse.sentenceFrame: When converting from a ___ unit to a ___ unit, I ___ by the conversion factor because ___.

approaching.stem: How many inches are in 7 feet?
choiceFeedback: Multiply 7 by 12 (inches per foot).
There are 12 inches in every foot.
You multiplied by 8 feet. Re-read how many feet the question gives.
hints: The key fact: 1 foot = 12 inches. You have 7 feet and want inches.
Going from a BIGGER unit (feet) to a SMALLER unit (inches) means you multiply.
Set up 7 × 12 — seven groups of 12 inches.
hintsEs: El dato clave: 1 pie = 12 pulgadas. Tienes 7 pies y quieres pulgadas.
Ir de una unidad MAYOR (pies) a una MENOR (pulgadas) significa que multiplicas.
Plantea 7 × 12: siete grupos de 12 pulgadas.

approaching.stem: How many feet are in 3 yards?
choiceFeedback: Multiply 3 by 3 (feet per yard).
There are 3 feet in every yard.
Not quite. 1 yard = 3 feet.
hints: The key fact: 1 yard = 3 feet. You have 3 yards and want feet.
Big unit (yards) to small unit (feet) means multiply by the conversion factor 3.
Set up 3 × 3 — three yards, each worth 3 feet.
hintsEs: El dato clave: 1 yarda = 3 pies. Tienes 3 yardas y quieres pies.
De unidad grande (yardas) a unidad pequeña (pies) significa multiplicar por el factor de conversión 3.
Plantea 3 × 3: tres yardas, cada una de 3 pies.

approaching.stem: How many ounces are in 4 pounds?
choiceFeedback: Multiply 4 by 16 (ounces per pound).
There are 16 ounces in every pound.
Not quite. 1 pound = 16 ounces.
hints: The key fact: 1 pound = 16 ounces. You have 4 pounds and want ounces.
Pounds are bigger than ounces, so converting to ounces means multiplying by 16.
Set up 4 × 16. (Break it up: 4 × 10 = 40 and 4 × 6 = 24, then add.)
hintsEs: El dato clave: 1 libra = 16 onzas. Tienes 4 libras y quieres onzas.
Las libras son mayores que las onzas, así que convertir a onzas significa multiplicar por 16.
Plantea 4 × 16. (Sepáralo: 4 × 10 = 40 y 4 × 6 = 24, y luego suma.)

choiceFeedback: Divide 24 by 12 (inches per foot).
There are 12 inches in one foot.
That is the number of inches. Going from inches to feet means dividing.
hints: This one goes the OTHER direction: inches (small) to feet (big), so the number of units gets smaller.
Small unit to big unit means divide. Ask: how many groups of 12 inches fit in 24 inches?
Set up 24 ÷ 12.
hintsEs: Esta va en la dirección CONTRARIA: de pulgadas (pequeña) a pies (grande), así que el número de unidades se hace menor.
De unidad pequeña a unidad grande significa dividir. Pregunta: ¿cuántos grupos de 12 pulgadas caben en 24 pulgadas?
Plantea 24 ÷ 12.

approaching.title: Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Convert 2 yards of rope to feet

approaching.correctWork: Feet are smaller than yards, so you multiply (not divide): 2 × 3 = 6 feet. Changing to a smaller unit always gives a bigger number, not a tiny decimal.
hints: You are going from a bigger unit (yards) to a smaller unit (feet). Should the number get bigger or smaller?
Changing to a smaller unit means more of them, so multiply: 2 × 3 = 6 feet.
approaching.explanation: The Operate step divided when it should have multiplied. Feet are smaller than yards, so each yard becomes 3 feet and 2 × 3 = 6 feet. The answer 0.67 feet is a warning sign by itself — a 2-yard rope cannot end up shorter than 1 foot.
approaching.explanationEs: En el paso de operar se dividió cuando había que multiplicar. Los pies son más pequeños que las yardas, así que cada yarda se vuelve 3 pies y 2 × 3 = 6 pies. La respuesta de 0.67 pies es una señal de alerta por sí sola: una cuerda de 2 yardas no puede quedar más corta que 1 pie.

approaching.stem: A shelf is 30 inches long. How many feet and inches is that?
choiceFeedback: Divide by 12 and look for a remainder: 30 ÷ 12 = 2 R6.
Find how many complete feet fit, then how many inches left over.
18 inches is more than a foot, so this answer is not finished. Keep taking out groups of 12 inches until fewer than 12 remain.
hints: 30 inches is more than 2 feet (24 in) but less than 3 feet (36 in) — so the answer is 2 feet plus some leftover inches.
Divide by 12 to find whole feet; the REMAINDER stays as inches.
Compute 30 ÷ 12: it goes in 2 whole times using up 24 inches. Subtract 30 − 24 to find the leftover inches.
approaching.stemEs: Un estante mide 30 pulgadas de largo. ¿A cuántos pies y pulgadas equivale?
approaching.explanationEs: 30 ÷ 12 = 2 y sobran 6. Entonces 30 pulgadas = 2 pies 6 pulgadas.
hintsEs: 30 pulgadas es más de 2 pies (24 pulg) pero menos de 3 pies (36 pulg), así que la respuesta es 2 pies más unas pulgadas sobrantes.
Divide entre 12 para hallar los pies enteros; el RESIDUO se queda como pulgadas.
Calcula 30 ÷ 12: cabe 2 veces enteras usando 24 pulgadas. Resta 30 − 24 para hallar las pulgadas sobrantes.

onLevel.stem: Leg 1: The joystick rod is 3 feet long, but the parts catalog lists it in inches. How many inches is that? (1 ft = 12 in)
onLevel.explanation: Inches are smaller than feet, so multiply: 3 × 12 = 36 inches.
choiceFeedback: Multiply by 12 (inches per foot).
How many inches per foot?
Check the conversion factor: a foot is 12 inches, not 11. Multiply the number of feet by 12.
onLevel.stemEs: Tramo 1: La barra de la palanca de mando mide 3 pies de largo, pero el catálogo de piezas la lista en pulgadas. ¿A cuántas pulgadas equivale? (1 pie = 12 pulgadas)
onLevel.explanationEs: Las pulgadas son más pequeñas que los pies, así que multiplica: 3 × 12 = 36 pulgadas.
hints: Converting to a smaller unit always produces a larger count of those units.
Decide whether to multiply or divide: inches are smaller than feet, so the number goes up.
Use the factor 1 ft = 12 in and set up 3 × 12. Finish that multiplication to get the length in inches.
hintsEs: Convertir a una unidad más pequeña siempre produce una cantidad mayor de esas unidades.
Decide si multiplicar o dividir: las pulgadas son más pequeñas que los pies, así que el número aumenta.
Usa el factor 1 pie = 12 pulgadas y plantea 3 × 12. Termina esa multiplicación para obtener la longitud en pulgadas.

onLevel.stem: Leg 2: A power cable on the cabinet plan measures 2.5 kilometers across the whole arcade network. How many meters is that? (1 km = 1,000 m)
onLevel.explanation: Meters are smaller than kilometers, so multiply: 2.5 × 1,000 = 2,500 meters.
choiceFeedback: Multiply by 1000.
1000 meters per kilometer.
That is a multiplication by 10,000 instead of 1,000. There are 1,000 meters in a kilometer, so the digits shift three places, not four.
onLevel.stemEs: Tramo 2: Un cable de energía en el plano del gabinete mide 2.5 kilómetros a lo largo de toda la red de la sala de juegos. ¿A cuántos metros equivale? (1 km = 1,000 m)
onLevel.explanationEs: Los metros son más pequeños que los kilómetros, así que multiplica: 2.5 × 1,000 = 2,500 metros.
hints: A kilometer is much longer than a meter, so the number of meters will be much larger than 2.5.
Multiply by the conversion factor, because you are moving to a smaller unit.
Set up 2.5 × 1,000. Multiplying by 1,000 shifts the decimal point three places — move it and read the result.
hintsEs: Un kilómetro es mucho más largo que un metro, así que la cantidad de metros será mucho mayor que 2.5.
Multiplica por el factor de conversión, porque estás pasando a una unidad más pequeña.
Plantea 2.5 × 1,000. Multiplicar por 1,000 mueve el punto decimal tres lugares: muévelo y lee el resultado.

onLevel.stem: Leg 3: The coin box weighs 5 pounds, but the shipping label needs the weight in ounces. How many ounces is that? (1 lb = 16 oz)
onLevel.explanation: Ounces are smaller than pounds, so multiply: 5 × 16 = 80 ounces.
choiceFeedback: Multiply by 16 (ounces per pound).
How many ounces per pound?
That is the number of ounces in a single pound. The box weighs 5 pounds, so the conversion factor still has to be applied to all of them.
onLevel.stemEs: Tramo 3: La caja de monedas pesa 5 libras, pero la etiqueta de envío necesita el peso en onzas. ¿A cuántas onzas equivale? (1 libra = 16 onzas)
onLevel.explanationEs: Las onzas son más pequeñas que las libras, así que multiplica: 5 × 16 = 80 onzas.
hints: Ounces are smaller than pounds, so 5 pounds turns into many more ounces.
Multiply the number of pounds by the number of ounces in one pound.
Write 5 × 16 and finish it. Breaking it up helps: 5 × 10 plus 5 × 6.
hintsEs: Las onzas son más pequeñas que las libras, así que 5 libras se convierten en muchas más onzas.
Multiplica la cantidad de libras por la cantidad de onzas que tiene una libra.
Escribe 5 × 16 y termínalo. Separarlo ayuda: 5 × 10 más 5 × 6.

onLevel.title: Level 2 Extension — Multiply or Divide?

workedExample.label: Convert 4 feet of side panel to inches

onLevel.correctWork: Inches are smaller than feet, so you multiply (not divide): 4 × 12 = 48 inches. The answer should be larger, not smaller, when changing to a smaller unit.
hints: You are going from a larger unit (feet) to a smaller unit (inches). Should the number get bigger or smaller?
Changing to a smaller unit means more of them, so multiply: 4 × 12 = 48 inches.
onLevel.explanation: The Operate step divided when the conversion calls for multiplying. Inches are smaller than feet, so each of the 4 feet becomes 12 inches: 4 × 12 = 48 inches. A side panel measuring 0.33 inches would be smaller than a fingertip, which is another sign the operation was flipped.
onLevel.explanationEs: En el paso de operar se dividió cuando la conversión pide multiplicar. Las pulgadas son más pequeñas que los pies, así que cada uno de los 4 pies se vuelve 12 pulgadas: 4 × 12 = 48 pulgadas. Un panel lateral de 0.33 pulgadas sería más pequeño que la punta de un dedo, otra señal de que se invirtió la operación.

onLevel.stem: Final Leg: The finished cabinet ships in a crate holding 8 quarts of packing gel, but the supplier sells gel by the gallon. How many gallons is that? (4 qt = 1 gal)
onLevel.explanation: Gallons are bigger than quarts, so divide: 8 ÷ 4 = 2 gallons.
choiceFeedback: Divide by 4 (quarts per gallon).
4 quarts per gallon.
That looks like 8 + 4 rather than a conversion. Quarts are smaller than gallons, so the number of gallons has to come out smaller than 8.
onLevel.stemEs: Tramo final: El gabinete terminado se envía en una caja con 8 cuartos de galón de gel de embalaje, pero el proveedor vende el gel por galón. ¿A cuántos galones equivale? (4 cuartos = 1 galón)
onLevel.explanationEs: Los galones son más grandes que los cuartos, así que divide: 8 ÷ 4 = 2 galones.
hints: Gallons are larger than quarts, so the number of gallons will be smaller than 8.
Moving to a larger unit means dividing by the conversion factor.
Set up 8 ÷ 4 using 4 qt = 1 gal, and finish the division.
hintsEs: Los galones son más grandes que los cuartos, así que la cantidad de galones será menor que 8.
Pasar a una unidad más grande significa dividir entre el factor de conversión.
Plantea 8 ÷ 4 usando 4 cuartos = 1 galón y termina la división.

onLevel.title: Find the Conversion Error
onLevel.correctWork: Since 3 feet = 1 yard, you divide by 3 (not multiply). 6 ÷ 3 = 2 yards.
hints: You're going from a smaller unit (feet) to a larger unit (yards). Should you multiply or divide?
Converting to a larger unit gives a smaller number. 6 feet ÷ 3 = 2 yards.
onLevel.explanation: Feet are smaller than yards, so 6 feet has to become a smaller number of yards, not a bigger one. Since 3 feet make 1 yard, divide: 6 ÷ 3 = 2 yards. Multiplying by 3 moved in the wrong direction and produced 18 yards, which is 9 times too long.
onLevel.explanationEs: Los pies son más pequeños que las yardas, así que 6 pies debe convertirse en un número menor de yardas, no mayor. Como 3 pies forman 1 yarda, se divide: 6 ÷ 3 = 2 yardas. Multiplicar por 3 fue en la dirección equivocada y dio 18 yardas, que es 9 veces demasiado largo.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Convert Measurement Units is applying the conversion factor in the wrong direction — for example, converting 4 feet to inches by dividing (4 ÷ 12 = 0.33 inches) instead of multiplying (4 × 12 = 48 inches), or converting 80 ounces to pounds by multiplying (80 × 16 = 1,280 pounds) instead of dividing (80 ÷ 16 = 5 pounds). Before you answer, ask: am I changing to a SMALLER unit (there will be MORE of them, so multiply) or a BIGGER unit (there will be FEWER of them, so divide)?

connect.scenario: The arcade is ordering a new game cabinet. The doorway is 80 inches tall. The cabinet is listed as 7 feet. Your friend says it won't fit because 7 feet is 82 inches.
connect.promptQuestion: Will the cabinet fit through the doorway? Show your conversion to prove it.
connect.prompt: 7 feet = 7 × ___ = ___ inches. Since ___ inches is ___ than 80 inches, the cabinet ___ fit through the doorway.

check.stem: How many inches are in 1 foot?
check.explanation: 1 foot = 12 inches. That is the conversion factor for this problem.

check.stem: How many inches tall is the 7-foot cabinet?
check.explanation: 7 × 12 = 84 inches. Your friend's 82 is close but not correct.

check.stem: Will the cabinet fit through the 80-inch doorway?
choices: You cannot tell without the width
check.explanation: 84 inches is taller than the 80-inch doorway, so it will not fit — your friend's conclusion was right even though the conversion was off by 2.

connect.modelAnswer: 7 feet = 7 × 12 = 84 inches, not 82. Since 84 inches is greater than the 80-inch doorway, the cabinet will not fit. Your friend reached the right conclusion but converted incorrectly — always multiply feet by 12 to get inches.

exitTicket.stem: Quick check — you've got this: Which is the correct conversion of 5 yards to inches?
exitTicket.explanation: 5 yards × 3 = 15 feet. 15 feet × 12 = 180 inches. Or: 5 × 36 = 180 inches.
choiceFeedback: Convert 5 yards to feet, then feet to inches.
Start with: 5 yards = ? feet. Then convert to inches.
Remember: 1 yard = 3 feet, and 1 foot = 12 inches.
hints: Yards to inches is a TWO-step trip: yards → feet → inches (or use 1 yard = 36 inches in one jump).
Multiply twice: yards × 3 gives feet, then feet × 12 gives inches. Or multiply yards × 36 directly.
Step 1: 5 × 3 = 15 feet. Step 2: multiply that 15 by 12 to land on inches.
